questions.question: In 2024, the city of Lenton planted shade trees along three blocks that had few mature trees. Summer pavement temperatures on those blocks fell by an average of 4°C, and pedestrians reported that the sidewalks felt more comfortable. The program requires regular watering during the trees' first two years, adding to maintenance costs. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Pedestrians in Lenton prefer walking only on streets with mature trees.
Watering young trees is the largest expense in Lenton's annual budget.
Pavement temperature is determined entirely by the number of nearby trees.
Lenton's tree-planting program produced measurable benefits but also created maintenance needs.
questions.explanation: D is correct because it captures both the program's benefits and its maintenance requirement. The other choices elevate a detail or make a claim the text does not support.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Marine biologists attached fragments of the same coral species to restoration frames at four reef sites. Survival rates differed sharply among the sites. When the researchers later matched coral strains to the temperature and water-flow conditions at each site, survival improved. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Matching coral strains to local conditions can improve restoration outcomes.
All coral strains survive equally well when attached to metal frames.
Water flow is the only factor that affects restored coral.
Coral restoration is possible only at four reef sites.
questions.explanation: A is correct. It expresses the passage's central finding, while the other choices misstate or overgeneralize individual details.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A public library extended its weekday hours from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. During the next three months, evening visits increased substantially, especially among adults who reported working during the day. The library board is now considering whether to make the schedule permanent. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The library board has already made the new schedule permanent.
Most daytime library visitors are adults who do not work.
Later hours appear to have expanded library access, particularly for working adults.
The library receives no visitors before 6 p.m.
questions.explanation: C is correct because it synthesizes the schedule change and the most important attendance result. The other options contradict or exaggerate secondary information.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Some bees release pollen by vibrating their flight muscles while gripping a flower. In an experiment, two bee species produced vibrations at different average frequencies, but both released similar amounts of pollen from the same plant species. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Only one bee species can release pollen by vibrating flowers.
Different vibration patterns can be similarly effective at releasing pollen.
The plant species in the experiment produces no pollen without bees.
Vibration frequency always determines how much pollen a bee releases.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The key result is that different average frequencies produced similar pollen release; the species and plant are supporting details.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Chemical analysis of pottery from an ancient coastal settlement showed that most vessels were made with local clay. Several vessels, however, contained decorative minerals found only in a region hundreds of kilometers inland. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: All pottery at the settlement was imported from inland communities.
Coastal potters avoided decorating vessels made from local clay.
The settlement had no access to materials from distant regions.
Local pottery production likely incorporated some materials obtained through long-distance exchange.
questions.explanation: D is correct because it combines the local-clay evidence with the presence of distant minerals. The other choices conflict with one or both findings.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: After a former parking area was restored as a wetland, the site held more stormwater during heavy rain and supported more bird species than it had previously. Managers must still remove invasive plants each spring to maintain those gains. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The restored wetland provides ecological and flood-control benefits that require continued management.
Removing invasive plants prevents all flooding near the former parking area.
Bird species avoid wetlands that are managed in the spring.
The parking area stored more stormwater than the restored wetland.
questions.explanation: A is correct because it captures the overall benefits and the need for upkeep. The other choices distort particular details.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: In one introductory programming course, students alternated between writing code and reviewing a partner's code. On later assignments, these students identified errors more accurately and explained their solutions more clearly than students who had practiced only writing code. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Reviewing code is useful only after students have mastered programming.
Students who write code should never work with a partner.
Alternating between producing and reviewing code may strengthen debugging and explanation skills.
The students who reviewed code completed fewer assignments.
questions.explanation: C is correct because it states the broad instructional implication supported by both reported outcomes. The remaining choices are unsupported or contradictory.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Sensors placed on a glacier initially reported rapid afternoon melting. Engineers discovered that direct sunlight was heating the sensors themselves. After the sensors were fitted with reflective shields, the afternoon readings aligned with measurements from nearby instruments. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Reflective shields cause glaciers to melt more slowly.
A measurement problem, rather than unusually rapid melting, explained the original sensor readings.
Nearby instruments cannot measure afternoon glacier conditions.
Glacier sensors produce reliable data only before noon.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The central point is that sunlight distorted the original measurements and that shielding corrected the problem.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A housing cooperative installed gardens on three flat roofs. The gardens reduced summer roof temperatures and absorbed some rainfall, but the cooperative had to reinforce one older roof before planting. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Every roof in the cooperative required complete reconstruction.
The gardens absorbed all rainfall that reached the buildings.
Rooftop gardens provided environmental benefits, although one building required structural preparation.
The cooperative removed its gardens after one summer.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice captures both the reported benefits and the limited structural challenge instead of isolating one detail.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Speakers of the Nami language created weekly conversation groups and recorded elders telling traditional stories. After two years, more teenagers could hold basic conversations, though few had yet reached advanced fluency. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Teenagers became fully fluent after attending one meeting.
The recorded stories replaced the conversation groups.
Only elders were permitted to speak Nami.
Community programs increased basic Nami use among teenagers, while advanced fluency remained uncommon.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice includes the program's progress and its remaining limitation.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Researchers placed coconut shells and plain stones in an aquarium with octopuses. Several octopuses carried the shells and later assembled them as shelters, whereas they rarely moved the stones. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The octopuses selectively transported objects that could later serve as shelter.
The octopuses used stones more often than shells.
All aquarium objects were immediately eaten.
The shells changed the temperature of the aquarium.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The choice summarizes the meaningful contrast between carrying useful shells and rarely moving stones.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A neighborhood installed low sound barriers beside a busy road. Measurements showed that the barriers reduced noise on ground-floor patios but had little effect on upper-floor balconies. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The barriers eliminated traffic on the road.
The barriers reduced road noise at lower elevations but were less effective higher up.
Upper-floor balconies were quieter before the barriers were installed.
The barriers reduced noise equally at every height.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The choice states the overall finding and the important difference by elevation.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Excavations revealed that an ancient road was repaired repeatedly with local stone. Pottery from distant regions was found beside several repair layers, suggesting that travelers continued using the route over many generations. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The road was built entirely from pottery.
Travel stopped after the first repair.
Repeated repairs and imported pottery indicate that the road remained an active route for a long period.
Only local goods moved along the road.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice integrates the repair and pottery evidence into the passage's central historical conclusion.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A university café introduced reusable cups with a refundable deposit. Disposable-cup use fell sharply, but many reusable cups were not returned until the café added collection bins in residence halls. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The café stopped serving drinks after introducing deposits.
Residence halls prohibited reusable cups.
Disposable-cup use increased when collection bins were added.
The deposit program reduced disposable-cup use, and convenient return locations improved the reusable system.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice captures both the initial success and the operational improvement.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A regional seed bank stores duplicate seed samples in two buildings with separate power systems. The arrangement costs more than using one facility, but it reduces the chance that a single equipment failure will destroy an entire collection. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Duplicating storage increases cost but protects the seed collection from a single failure.
The two buildings share one power system.
Equipment failures cannot affect stored seeds.
The seed bank plans to discard duplicate samples.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The choice identifies the main tradeoff rather than focusing only on cost or location.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A warehouse tested robots that choose routes independently rather than following fixed floor markings. The new robots adjusted more quickly when aisles were blocked, although they required more computing power. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Fixed floor markings use more computing power than route planning.
Independent route planning improved flexibility but increased computing demands.
Blocked aisles caused every robot to stop permanently.
The warehouse removed all aisles during the test.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The choice summarizes the benefit and cost of the new routing approach.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A museum lowered light levels around delicate textiles and added focused lamps that activate when visitors approach. The textiles now receive less total light, while visitors report that labels remain easy to read. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The museum removed all labels from the textile exhibit.
Visitors preferred the exhibit only when every lamp stayed on.
Responsive lighting reduced textile exposure without making the exhibit difficult to view.
Focused lamps increased the textiles' total light exposure.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice captures the conservation goal and the maintained visitor experience.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Trees in one forest exchanged carbon with nearby seedlings through fungal networks. The transfers were small compared with the carbon seedlings produced themselves, but they increased when seedlings were heavily shaded. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Seedlings obtained all their carbon from fungal networks.
Carbon transfer stopped when seedlings were shaded.
Trees transferred equal amounts under every condition.
Fungal networks supplied limited carbon to seedlings, with larger transfers under deep shade.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice preserves both the small scale of the transfers and the shade-related increase.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: After a city reduced bus fares on weekends, ridership increased most on routes serving parks and shopping districts. Weekday ridership changed little because weekday fares remained the same. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Lower weekend fares increased weekend travel, especially to recreational and shopping destinations.
Weekday fares were eliminated throughout the city.
Ridership fell on every route serving a park.
The fare change affected weekday and weekend travel equally.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The choice states the main effect and where it was strongest.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A translator preserved the short lines of a poem but changed several images that would have been obscure to readers in the target language. The translation therefore resembles the original rhythm more closely than its imagery. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The translator reproduced every image word for word.
The translator prioritized the poem's rhythmic form while adapting some of its imagery.
The translation abandoned the poem's short lines.
Readers in the target language rejected all poetic imagery.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The choice describes the translator's central tradeoff between form and imagery.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Farmers near a dormant volcano noticed that fields containing thin layers of old volcanic ash retained water longer than nearby sandy fields. Very thick ash layers, however, restricted root growth. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Any amount of volcanic ash prevents plants from growing.
Sandy fields always retain more water than ash-rich fields.
Volcanic ash can improve water retention in moderate amounts but hinder roots when too thick.
Root growth determines whether a volcano becomes active.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice captures the contrasting effects associated with ash depth.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: On reefs where large predatory fish returned after fishing limits were introduced, some smaller fish spent more time close to coral shelter. Their overall population still increased because the reefs also contained more food and healthier coral. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Small fish disappeared when predators returned.
Fishing limits reduced both food and coral health.
Small fish never use coral as shelter.
Predator recovery changed small-fish behavior, while broader reef improvements supported their population growth.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice combines the behavioral response with the population trend and its context.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A mill began recycling paper fibers more times before discarding them. This reduced demand for new pulp, but fibers became shorter with each cycle and eventually had to be mixed with fresh material. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Repeated recycling conserves new pulp but eventually requires fresh fibers to maintain paper quality.
Paper fibers become longer every time they are recycled.
The mill eliminated the use of fresh material entirely.
Recycled fibers cannot be used to make paper.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The choice states the resource benefit and the material limitation.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A high school shifted its start time forty minutes later. Students reported sleeping longer on school nights, while participation in early-morning clubs declined until the clubs were rescheduled. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Students slept less after the schedule changed.
A later start increased reported sleep but required adjustments to morning activities.
Every club was permanently canceled.
The school moved its start time earlier by forty minutes.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The choice summarizes the benefit and the scheduling consequence.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Biologists compared satellite images with field surveys to count seals on remote beaches. Images allowed more beaches to be checked, but field surveys were still needed where rocks and shadows resembled animals. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Satellite images clearly distinguished every seal from every rock.
Field surveys could reach more beaches than satellites could image.
Satellite images expanded survey coverage, while field checks remained necessary in visually ambiguous locations.
Biologists stopped counting seals on remote beaches.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice captures the complementary strengths and limitations of both methods.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Urban bats used newly installed roost boxes most often when the boxes faced morning sun but were shaded in the afternoon. Boxes exposed to sun all day became too warm during summer. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Bats selected only boxes exposed to all-day sun.
Afternoon shade caused every box to become too warm.
The direction a roost box faces has no effect on its temperature.
Roost-box placement that balances morning warmth and afternoon shade appears most suitable for bats.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice synthesizes the use pattern and the temperature evidence.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: An open-source microscope can be assembled from widely available parts, allowing schools to repair it locally. Its images are less detailed than those from advanced laboratory microscopes but sufficient for many introductory lessons. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The open-source microscope trades some image detail for affordability and repairability in basic instruction.
The open-source microscope produces the most detailed images available.
Schools cannot obtain replacement parts for the microscope.
Introductory lessons require advanced laboratory equipment.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The choice captures the device's practical advantage and technical limitation.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A town sends household food scraps to a composting facility instead of a landfill. The program reduces landfill waste, but contamination from plastic bags slows processing and requires additional sorting. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Plastic bags speed the composting process.
Food-scrap composting reduces landfill waste but works better when plastic contamination is controlled.
The town sends all household waste directly to the landfill.
Additional sorting increases food-scrap contamination.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The choice summarizes both the program's benefit and its operational challenge.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: Historians compared several maps of the same nineteenth-century harbor. Later maps show new warehouses but omit small fishing docks still mentioned in tax records, indicating that mapmakers emphasized different features for different users. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tax records prove that the warehouses never existed.
Every map displayed all harbor features with equal detail.
Differences among the maps reflect changing purposes as well as physical changes in the harbor.
Small fishing docks appeared only on the latest maps.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice accounts for both newly mapped warehouses and deliberately omitted docks.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息

questions.question: A lecture hall installed wall panels that absorb echoes. Students seated at the back reported clearer speech, while students near the front noticed little change because speech had already been clear there. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The panels made speech less clear in every seat.
Front-row students could not hear before the panels were installed.
The panels changed the content of the lectures.
Acoustic panels improved speech clarity mainly in the part of the room that previously had the greatest problem.
questions.explanation: D is correct. The choice identifies the overall effect and why it differed by seating area.
questions.teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
